summary: 16 context-isolated runs (8 questions × Fable 5.1 / Opus 5), scored 0–2 on five criteria. Both models produced correct, honest, numerically consistent answers on every question, including the three unseen ones (inflation, New York flu, private website traffic) and both Hebrew questions (answered in English). Identical forecasts where the pipeline decides (unemployment 4.1 % ±0.2, flu nowcast 1.69 %, S&P drift ~7,741, Israel 3.1 % ±0.4, CPI +0.27…0.31 % m/m). Differences were in depth, not correctness: Opus wrote richer case-specific caveats and found more skill defects; Fable was faster and equally disciplined. Every defect reported by either model was fixed before the final skill version (17 fixes, listed in research/conclusions.md §10).
